notes: The 1986 volume of the Recreation and Park Commission; the scan holds only September to December meetings. Curated: plans and the Coit Tower restoration contract.

coverage.remaining: January-August 1986 minutes are not in the scanned volume (only its index): the Grove R. Mohr diamond at St. Mary's (Res. 14221), the Hall of Flowers renamed the San Francisco County Fair Building (Res. 14233) and Tea Garden Drive renamed Hagiwara Tea Garden Drive (Res. 14240) are known from the index only. Also not placed: St. Francis Yacht Club locker building (Ted Eden), Buena Vista Park master plan.
coverage.note: Dated by footers. Curated list F1986.py.

findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission gave conceptual approval to enlarging the field house at Alice Chalmers Playground, Brunswick and Whittier Streets, for its crowded tiny-tot and senior programs, designed by Peter Moy of Finger and Moy, architects, with a larger meeting room and kitchen, accessible restrooms and a clerestory to light the middle of the building.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, September 18, 1986

findings.address_as_written: Golden Gate Park Sharon Building Restoration Plans
findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission gave conceptual approval to the third phase of the Sharon Building's restoration, drawn by the Bureau of Architecture, which put the exterior first: cleaning, replacing and waterproofing the sandstone, with new wood doors, metal gates and window grilles at the lower level.

findings.address_as_written: Coit Tower Restoration - award of contract
findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission ratified a $527,194 contract with Nibbi-Lowe Construction Co. to restore Coit Tower, with a new roof and observation decks, elevator safety work and the sandblasting, treating and coating of the whole structure, after which the frescoes were to be restored and protected; the Commission also sought $64,415 in 1984 State Bond Act funds for the murals.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, October 16, 1986, Resolution No. 14510
